_readme: RATCHET. Prompts that were already staged when the `module` gate landed and whose module cannot be derived from `scope`. An entry downgrades MODULE_AMBIGUOUS from a REJECT to a WARNING so the prompt still lints ADMIT and still arms. THIS FILE MAY ONLY SHRINK. Entries may be REMOVED, never ADDED: adding one is the gate failing open, and the correct fix for a new prompt is to add `module: <name>` to its front matter (see docs/pr-prompts/PROMPT-SCHEMA.md#module). MEASURED 2026-09-07 over all 107 tracked -HOLD.md/-ready.md prompts under docs/pr-prompts/ excluding superseded/ and archive/: 64 derive one product module, 13 resolve to a sole incidental destination (prisma/docs/ci/e2e/sot/board) - 77 of 107 (72%) need no author input - and the 30 listed here do not. Keyed by SLUG, not filename: arm-prompt.ps1 renames <slug>-HOLD.md to <slug>-ready.md, so a baseline keyed by the HOLD filename would stop matching at the exact moment of arming and turn an ADMIT into a REJECT during the arm it exists to protect. Shape mirrors docs/qa/sot-refs-baseline.json ({_readme, entries}) so there is one baseline pattern in this repo, not two. NOT YET CI-ENFORCED: there is no check-module-baseline-ratchet.mjs and no ci.yml step comparing this file's entry set against origin/main, so 'may only shrink' is currently a convention a reviewer must enforce by eye. Wiring that (alongside check-sot-baseline-ratchet.mjs, which does exactly this for the sot baseline) is the obvious next slice. Do NOT write a count of remaining entries into this prose: entries.length is the count.
